newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 6.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Bill Clinton has won a second presidential term in a landslide victory which owed much to the US female vote. Despite this America will have a divided government. Republicans will continue to control the House of Representatives but with a reduced majority, which will constrain any radical presidential initiatives as well as ensure that White House scandals are investigated.

As results of the US elections showed that Americans have opted to divide power between a Democratic president and a Republican Congress, Wall Street declared victory. A Republican Congress has ensured that there will be 'no new worries about the deficit, no new legacy expenditures, no big funded tax cuts' according to Thomas McManus of Morgan Stanley in New York.

Despite earlier speculation that he wanted to sell his company's stake in Fairfax newspapers, Conrad Black chief of Hollinger International, has decided instead to up his company's stake in the Australian group from 25 per cent to 50 percent.
DOLLAR GETS THE FAR EAST VOTE

As news got through that the Republican party kept control of the Senate, the value of the dollar increased in Far East trading. Against the Japanese currency the greenback gained three-fifths of a yen to 114.5 and almost a pfennig against the Deutschmark to 1.525.
EMAP BIDS TO SHOW REBEL PAIR THE DOOR

At a meeting next month the media group EMAP are to debate a single resolution, to remove two non-executive directors of the company. The two men decided to stand against fellow directors at a meeting in July and at a board meeting a fortnight ago brought forward proposals to oust the chairman and chief executive from the board. EMAP is set to mail shareholders with a circulation on the resolution today.
